newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission confirms Irish, Greek green rates to devalue.
newsitem.headline: Commission confirms Irish, Greek green rates to devalue.

text.p: The green rates of the Irish pound and the Greek drachma will be devalued with effect from Friday, the European Commission confirmed.
The green Irish pound will be devalued to 0.757666 per Ecu, compared with the current rate of 0.756658, and the green Greek drachma will be devalued to 311.858 per Ecu compared with 311.761.

The UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) earlier on Thursday forecast the devaluations after both countries averaged a negative monetary gap -- the difference between green and market rates -- during the May 6 - May 15 reference period.
Green rates are used by the European Union to convert Ecus into the currencies of its member states in its Common Agricultural Policy.
